comparison: Both evaluate dataset composition claims (C3, C40, C41, C96, C97, C98) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes internal consistency and documentation, while peer reviewers highlight comprehensiveness and methodological rigor. Peer result also includes C42, C43 (phylogenetic claims). Strong agreement on dataset quality.

Both evaluate geographical AMR distribution claims (C4, C5, C54-C59) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on genomic data demonstrating MDR prevalence in North America and plasmid associations. Peer reviewers affirm these as core contributions showing clonal expansions linked to geography. Peer result also includes C6 (Australian isolates). Strong agreement.

OpenEval evaluates C6 (Australian isolates with minimal AMR) as SUPPORTED based on resistance profiling. Peer result R2 includes C6 among broader geographical AMR findings and affirms it as part of rigorous characterization. Agreement on this specific finding.

Both evaluate phylogenetic lineage separation claims (C7, C9, C10, C43, C46-C49) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes phylogenetic analysis and BAPS clustering. Peer reviewers affirm detailed genomic epidemiology and evolutionary history. Peer result also includes C8, C50-C53 (plasmid and dating claims). Strong agreement on phylogenetic findings.

Both evaluate plasmid characterization claims (C63, C64) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on long-read sequencing showing replicon types and absence of spv operon. Peer result R8 includes these within broader plasmid analysis (C60-C64) and affirms novel recombinant plasmid discovery. Agreement on plasmid findings.

Both evaluate comparative genomic claims (C11, C85-C88) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes pangenome analysis showing distinct gene content and increased genome size in ST74. Peer reviewers affirm comparative analyses showing unique genetic content per genotype. Peer result also includes C12, C73, C95. Strong agreement.

OpenEval evaluates SPI-19 absence and SPI-6 truncation claims (C12, C73, C74) as SUPPORTED based on genomic analysis. Peer result R4 includes C12, C73 within broader comparative genomics and affirms these findings. Agreement on virulence island differences.

Both evaluate macrophage replication claims (C13, C75-C77) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes in vitro infection assays showing ST74 enhanced replication with statistical significance. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm ST74 replicates better intracellularly in macrophages. Strong agreement on phenotypic findings.

Both evaluate reduced cytotoxicity and inflammatory response claims (C14, C80, C83, C84) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes LDH and IL-1β assays showing reduced host cell death for ST74. Peer reviewers affirm differential responses and cytotoxicity findings. Peer result also includes C81. Strong agreement.

Both evaluate epithelial cell replication claims (C78, C79, C82) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes contrasting patterns in HT-29 cells with ST10 replicating better. Peer reviewers affirm these as part of cell-type specific differences in phenotypic characterization. Peer result also includes C81. Agreement.

Both evaluate Vi antigen absence claims (C15, C35, C72, C92) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes genomic screening showing viaB operon only in one historical isolate. Peer reviewers accept this as part of comprehensive genomic characterization with diagnostic implications. Perfect claim overlap and agreement.

OpenEval evaluates phylodynamic dating claims (C50-C53) as SUPPORTED based on Bayesian analysis with appropriate models. Peer result R3 includes these claims within broader phylogenetic findings and affirms evolutionary history analysis. Agreement on temporal estimates.

Both evaluate heavy metal resistance claims (C60, C62) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes genomic screening showing gold resistance genes and plasmid replicons. Peer result R8 includes these within broader plasmid and AMR characterization. Agreement on HMR patterns.

OpenEval evaluates invasiveness prediction claims (C66, C67) as UNCERTAIN, noting contradiction between bioinformatic predictions and in vitro data showing enhanced ST74 replication. Peer result R9 evaluates these as SUPPORTED within broader genomic characterization. Disagreement: OpenEval questions prediction tool validity while peer reviewers accept findings.

Both evaluate virulence determinant distribution claims (C68-C71) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes genomic screening showing differential distribution between lineages. Peer reviewers affirm these as part of rigorous virulence characterization. Peer result also includes C66, C67, C74. Agreement on virulence factors.

OpenEval evaluates spv operon speculation (C65) as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of direct experimental evidence linking absence to reduced invasiveness. Peer reviewers evaluate as SUPPORTED, accepting it as appropriate speculation based on cited literature. Disagreement: OpenEval more cautious about speculative interpretation than peer reviewers.

Both evaluate historical livestock movement claims (C89, C90) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes connection is inferential rather than directly demonstrated. Peer reviewers affirm insights into global spread and region-specific traits. Agreement with both acknowledging inferential nature.

Both evaluate fliC profile claim (C91) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes citation support and consistency with codon profile data. Peer reviewers accept this within broader contextual findings. Agreement on this background claim.

Both evaluate clinical presentation claims (C93, C94) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes small ST74 sample size (n=7) limits generalizability. Peer reviewers affirm clinical diversity findings as supporting importance of studying beyond lab strains. Perfect claim overlap and agreement.

OpenEval evaluates ST74-specific gene claim (C95) as SUPPORTED based on pangenome analysis. Peer result R4 includes C95 within broader comparative genomics showing unique genetic content. Agreement on this finding.

Both evaluate background/contextual claims (C1, C2, C16-C25) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes these are appropriately cited literature claims establishing scientific context. Peer reviewers implicitly accept background characterization without questioning. Agreement on contextual framework.

OpenEval evaluates additional background claims (C26-C30, C33, C34, C36-C39) as SUPPORTED based on citations. Peer result R11 includes many of these and affirms contextual framework, noting improved Discussion comparison with other serotypes. Agreement on literature-based context.
